# Five interval fibers: an exact fixed-support barrier and augmentation escape

The universal joint-endpoint-removal claim is false. More strongly, there is a strict local minimum of actual normalized depth among compatible five-fiber arrays, modulo continuous affine shear and scaling. The scope is continuous variation of sampled interval endpoints on fixed integer support. It is NOT an asserted local minimum in ambient-body Hausdorff topology: positive slices on a projection boundary can jump under that topology.

A separate explicit augmentation, given below, defeats this fixed-support minimum. It adds point fibers at two new integer bases without changing mass or depth, then grows them at coordinated rates. The proof retains every new candidate using one finite cap cover.

## 1. Actual body and exact baseline depth

At bases i=0,...,4 take the centered intervals of lengths

    w=(13,11,9,7,5),
    Ki=[-w_i/2,w_i/2].                                (1)

Both endpoint roofs are affine. Their convex hull C is an actual trapezoid of base projection [0,4], with exactly these positive integer fibers. Its mixed mass is M=45.

For p=1 or2, the upward cap through (p,0), with line x=a(z-p), has mass

    F_p(a)=sum_i clamp(w_i/2-a(i-p),0,w_i).            (2)

Its reverse has mass45-F_p(a). The complete knot tables are:

| p=1: a | F_1(a) |
|---|---:|
| -13/2 | 53/2 |
| -9/2 | 57/2 |
| -7/4 | 57/2 |
| -5/6 | 80/3 |
| 5/6 | 55/3 |
| 7/4 | 33/2 |
| 9/2 | 33/2 |
| 13/2 | 37/2 |

| p=2: a | F_2(a) |
|---|---:|
| -11/2 | 33/2 |
| -7/2 | 37/2 |
| -13/4 | 37/2 |
| -5/4 | 45/2 |
| 5/4 | 45/2 |
| 13/4 | 53/2 |
| 7/2 | 53/2 |
| 11/2 | 57/2 |

These are every possible knot a=±w_i/[2(i-p)], i!=p. Between knots F_p is affine, and the far tails are constant. Thus BOTH marks (1,0),(2,0) have exact raw depth33/2 against every nonvertical cap. Pure base caps contain their entire own fiber and the relevant whole side; their masses are larger.

For an upper certificate, the two caps

    x-2(z-1)>=0,      -x-2(z-1)>=0                  (3)

each have mass33/2 and cover every line over z<=1. Their proper sampled sections are exactly0,1,2. The two caps

    x+10(z-2)>=0,     -x+10(z-2)>=0                 (4)

each have mass33/2 and cover every line over z>=2. Their only proper sampled section is2; they contain fibers3,4 and miss0,1. Hence these four caps cover the whole mixed set. Consequently

    Q=33/2,        beta=Q/M=11/30.                  (5)

The outer fiber maxima are13/2 and5/2. At base3, two sufficiently tilted caps through its interval midpoint have mass7/2+5=17/2 and cover its whole plane. Thus only bases1,2 are deepest. Within each, the opposite continuous normals of its covering pair force the displayed point to be the unique maximizer. This does not import a two-source assertion from a smoothed model.

## 2. Exact depth in a full neighborhood of the five sampled fibers

Now perturb every sampled endpoint continuously. Let the positive widths be w_i and centers c_i. For all sufficiently small perturbations of (1), set

    y1=(c0+c1+c2)/3,     y2=c2,
    q1=(w0+w1+w2)/2,
    q2=w2/2+w3+w4.                                  (6)

The EXACT actual maximum is

    Q=max(q1,q2).                                    (7)

Here are the all-normal and all-candidate reasons, including the cap switches.

At source1 the two caps (3), shifted to pass through (1,y1), continue to cut fibers0,1,2 properly and to miss3,4. Their masses are

    sum_{i=0}^2 hi_i-3y1=q1,
    3y1-sum_{i=0}^2 lo_i=q1.

Their union still covers every line over z<=1. At source2 the caps (4), shifted to pass through (2,c2), still have massesq2 and cover every line over z>=2. This proves the global upper bound (7) for ALL candidate marks.

For the lower bounds, evaluate the complete knot lists at y1 and y2. Each knot is an affine function of the endpoint parameters with a fixed nonzero integer denominator. At the baseline all knots in each displayed table are distinct, and all noncritical values have a strict gap above the minimum and below the maximum. Their order therefore persists locally, as do all proper/full/empty statuses at knots.

At p=1 the two minimum knots bound the same plateau with proper block0,1,2. On that entire plateau its value is sum hi_i-3y1=q1. The corresponding two maximum knots have value M-q1. Every other knot retains its strict gap, so the exact infimum and supremum are q1 and M-q1. At p=2 the two far plateaus have valuesq2 and M-q2; every finite noncritical knot retains its strict gap. These facts prove the all-normal lower bounds at (1,y1),(2,c2). Pure base gaps also persist. Since each of these values is attained, (7) follows.

This is an exact finite-chamber argument, not differentiability at a selected cap or an arbitrary choice of supporting-facet selectors. Supporting endpoint knots are retained in the full lists. For an explicit neighborhood one may take each original sampled endpoint within1/100 of its baseline value: knot shifts are at most2/100, their minimum baseline separation is1/4, and a crude bound on each five-term knot-mass change is less than55/100. The shifts of q1 orq2 are at most5/100, and the shifts of M-q1 or M-q2 are at most15/100. The resulting worst gap error70/100 is below the smallest noncritical baseline gap11/6.

## 3. The fixed-support local minimum

Compatibility implies that the width sequence is concave. Hence

    w0+w4<=2w2,      w1+w3<=2w2,
    M=sum_i w_i<=5w2.                               (8)

Using (6)-(7),

    3Q >= 2q1+q2 = M+w2/2 >= (11/10)M.

Therefore every sufficiently close compatible positive five-fiber family satisfies

    beta>=11/30.                                    (9)

Equality forces q1=q2 and equality in (8). A concave sequence with equality in these midpoint inequalities is affine: w_i=A+Bi. Then q1=q2 gives

    A=-(13/2)B,

so the widths are a positive multiple of(13,11,9,7,5). Moreover the lower endpoint sequence is convex and the upper endpoint sequence concave. If their difference w is affine, their second differences must both vanish. Thus both endpoint sequences, and therefore the center sequence, are affine. Equality families are exactly continuous affine shears/translations and positive fiber scalings of (1).

After fixing total mass and removing the affine center graph, (1) is consequently a strict isolated local minimum. This directly blocks a universal positive-fiber monotone deformation on this fixed support. Indeed a continuous path with nonincreasing normalized depth must remain on the equality orbit while it is nearby. The same local statement holds at every point of the orbit by affine invariance. After normalization, the orbit is one point, so an open-and-closed argument forces such a path to remain there as long as total mass stays positive and the five sampled fibers vary continuously. It cannot reach a vanished endpoint with some other fiber still positive.

This statement neither assumes nor constructs an attained global minimizer. In particular11/30>1/4, so a strict local minimum can lie well above the known one-integer, one-continuous lower bound.

## 4. No joint endpoint-removal rate works, even with endpoint translations

In the neighborhood of Section2, remove endpoint masses u,v>=0, keeping the three interior fibers fixed. Formula (7) gives exactly

    Q(u,v)=max(33/2-u/2,33/2-v),
    M(u,v)=45-u-v.                                  (10)

This is independent of how the remaining endpoint intervals are translated, provided the perturbation is small and compatible. The first source mark follows the endpoint-center change through y1; the second mark remains c2.

For beta not to increase from11/30, both source inequalities require

    u/2 >= (11/30)(u+v),
    v >= (11/30)(u+v).

Equivalently,

    4u>=11v,           19v>=11u.                    (11)

There is no nonzero solution u,v>=0: substituting the second lower bound into the first would give76u>=121u. Thus the missing variable is not merely a better endpoint rate or endpoint translation. Even arbitrary compatible interior roof perturbations meet the local barrier (9).

## 5. Add two point fibers without changing measured data

There is nevertheless an explicit support-augmentation escape. First adjoin the two point fibers

    K_{-1}={15/2},          K5={0}.                  (12)

Let C_* be the convex hull after adjoining the two point fibers (12). This can be done by a continuous actual body path with unchanged mixed measure. For0<=t<=1 take the nested Minkowski path

    C_t=(1-t)C+t C_*.                              (13)

The endpoint inequalities below show that C and C_* have exactly the same fibers at0,...,4. Since C subset C_t subset C_*, every C_t retains those fibers exactly. Its projection is[-t,4+t], so before t=1 there is no new integer base; at t=1 the new endpoint fibers are exactly the two points (12), with zero one-dimensional volume. Their depth is zero because an exposing pure base cap contains only that endpoint point. Thus mass, original depths, and the maximum (5) remain unchanged along (13).

One can check compatibility directly: the left point lies on the affine extension x=13/2-z of the original upper roof and above the corresponding lower extension; the right point lies between the two affine extensions at base5. The new outer lower slopes are no greater than the old lower slope1 on the left and no smaller on the right, and the upper slopes obey the reversed inequalities.

## 6. Coordinated growth of the new fibers gives actual descent

Keep all five original fibers fixed. For0<=u<3, grow the two new fibers as

    K_{-1}(u)=[15/2-u,15/2],
    K5(u)=[-u/4,u/4].                               (14)

Their masses are respectivelyu andu/2. The resulting seven sampled fibers are actual and complete. At the left, the new upper slope into base0 is-1, equal to the old upper slope, while the new lower slope is-14+u<=1. At the right, the new upper slope is u/4-5/2<=-1 and the new lower slope is5/2-u/4>=1. These are precisely the concavity/convexity inequalities. Total mass is

    M(u)=45+3u/2.                                    (15)

Shift the two left-covering caps to the common mark(1,u/6):

    x-2(z-1)>=u/6,
    -x-2(z-1)>=-u/6.                               (16)

Both continue to cut exactly the old fibers0,1,2 properly and to miss3,4,5. The first contains the new left fiber wholly. The second misses it, because

    15/2-u > 4+u/6   iff u<3.

The old proper-block contributions are33/2-u/2 and33/2+u/2 respectively. Adding the new-left mass to the first therefore makes BOTH cap masses

    33/2+u/2.                                       (17)

Their margins sum to-4(z-1), so their union covers every line over z<=1, including the new integer base-1.

Keep the two right-covering caps (4). Both miss the new left fiber, capture the new right fiber wholly, and retain all old statuses. Their masses are also (17). Their margins sum to20(z-2), so they cover every line over z>=2, including the new base5. These four caps therefore cover EVERY point of all seven actual integer fibers. Consequently

    beta_actual(u) <= B(u)
       =(33/2+u/2)/(45+3u/2),
    B'(u)=-(9/4)/(45+3u/2)^2 <0,
    B(u)<11/30 for every0<u<3.                      (18)

For example u=1 gives total mass93/2, a common cap budget17, and

    beta_actual <=34/93 <11/30,
    11/30-34/93=1/930.

This is a certified actual descent from the fixed-support minimum. It does not rely on all-normal lower classification of the perturbed body: an exact finite cover gives the required global upper bound, including all new candidate marks. Nor does (18) alone assert that the actual optimized depth is monotone at every pair of positive u-values; it provides a strictly decreasing common upper certificate and a strict improvement from the original body at everyu>0.

## 7. Meaning for the proposed deformation program

The stronger fixed-support monotone flow is false, already for five positive consecutive interval fibers. The obstruction is fully geometric, retains all cap directions and competing sources, and survives arbitrary small compatible sampled-endpoint perturbations. It is not a failure caused by choosing an unfavorable witness menu.

Support augmentation is a genuinely additional variable: the body can first move through unmeasured base positions to create two zero-mass integer fibers, then distribute new mass so both old source budgets increase more slowly than total mass. The shared-ratio calculation succeeds with additions precisely where the corresponding deletions fail. This one construction does not establish a universal augmentation theorem or an unrestricted bad-minimum reduction.

This is a pending mathematical submission, not an accepted fact. Its definitions, scoped assertions, calculations, and limitations are given in the proposed argument below. A reference to another pending candidate supplies context only; it is not an accepted premise.

# Five interval fibers: an exact fixed-support barrier and augmentation escape

**Five affine-width interval fibers form a fixed-support local minimum**

Centered interval widths (13,11,9,7,5) at bases 0,...,4 have maximum depth 11/30. In a sufficiently small compatible sampled-endpoint neighborhood the raw maximum is Q=max((w0+w1+w2)/2,w2/2+w3+w4). Discrete concavity implies Q/M>=11/30, with equality only for proportional affine widths and affine centers.

Scope limits: Strict local minimality is modulo shear/scaling and uses continuous sampled-endpoint topology on fixed positive bases. It is not Hausdorff local minimality among all ambient bodies.

**Coordinated fiber birth escapes the five-fiber barrier**

Keep the five old fibers of widths (13,11,9,7,5), add point fibers at (-1,15/2) and (5,0), and grow them to [15/2-u,15/2] and [-u/4,u/4], 0<u<3. Compatibility holds; four actual ambient caps cover every integer plane, each with mass 33/2+u/2. Total mass is 45+3u/2, so maximum depth is strictly below 11/30.

Scope limits: The certificate proves improvement from u=0, not pairwise monotonicity of actual optimized depth for all positive u. It is a concrete construction, not universal favorable birth.
